newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end lower on pre-holiday book-squaring.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end lower on pre-holiday book-squaring.

text.p: Key June Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended Monday's Tokyo session lower, pressured by selling from dealers who squared positions ahead of a Japanese national holiday on Tuesday, market sources said.
Most investors were reluctant to trade actively before the holiday.
Japan's financial markets will be closed on Tuesday.
June closed down 0.14 at 125.36. Turnover was 43,078 lots.
"June closed lower as dealers closed out positions near the end of the session. Most investors were unwilling to trade before the holiday," said a brokerage house trader.
Some players liquidated longs after the release of Japan's industrial production data for March in the mid-afternoon, which was better than the consensus forecast, traders said.
Production fell a preliminary 1.5 percent in March from the previous month on a seasonally adjusted basis, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said.
Most economists had predicted production would fall about 2.0 percent in March, traders said.
"The market has become quite sensitive to economic data indicative of the economy's strength," said a trader at a city bank's securities unit.
Traders said a positive outlook for production in April and May also weighed on JGBs.
MITI forecast that manufacturers' output would increase 1.9 percent month-on-month in April and another 1.1 percent in May.
"After seeing MITI's production outlook for April and May, people became more reluctant to test the upside," said the trader at the city bank's securities unit.

June fell to an intraday low of 125.20 shortly after the opening on the yen's weakness against the dollar that followed the weekend meeting of the Group of Seven (G7) finance ministers and central bank chiefs.
Open interest in the 123.00 put option stood at 1.3973 trillion yen, down from 1.4961 trillion yen on Friday.
"People are jittery because open interest in 123.00 put options is still high," said a brokerage house trader said.
In the cash JGB market, some investors were detected buying six-year JGBs and the 194th 10-year JGB.
"Investors were bargain-hunting these issues as their prices have fallen below par," said the brokerage house trader.
The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.295 percent, up from 2.265 percent on Friday.
